        - heading "Understand Inclusion-Exclusion" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "Inclusion-exclusion counts objects in overlapping sets without double-counting the overlap. A useful rule is Two-set inclusion-exclusion: |A union B| = |A| + |B| - |A intersection B|. You can learn Inclusion-Exclusion by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: Inclusion-exclusion counts objects in overlapping sets without double-counting the overlap. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, students: Count students in art or music. Watch out: Adding overlapping sets and keeping the overlap twice. Subtract the overlap once for two sets."
